To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
delta-lactoferring, a transcription factor, is covalently modified with SUMO-1 at five different lysines.
SUMOylation of the transcription factor delta-lactoferin controls both its transcriptional activity and its stability.
delta-lactoferring is a SUMOylation target.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the transcription factor delta-lactofertin, which is downregulated in breast cancer and possesses anti-proliferative activities.
the regulation of the expression of delta-lactoferin in normal and transformed cells.
the regulation of delta-lactoferin activity and stability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SUMOylation of Delta-lactofernin is a novel regulatory post-translational mechanism controlling both its stability and its transactivating function.
delta-lactoferring is a transcriptional regulator that is posttranslationally controlled by SUMOylation and other PTMs to modulate its stability and activity in response to specific stimuli.

SUMOylation is a new post-translational modification of the delta-lactoferring protein, that is a negative regulator of the transactivation capacity of delta-lactoferin, and that is a positive regulator of the stability of delta lactoferin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SUMOylation of a transcriptional factor may represent a general mechanism to repress its activity.
SUMOylation of K13 and K308 represses the transcriptional activity of delta-lactoferin and that K379 is a pivotal SUMO acceptor site that protects the protein against degradation.
SUMOylation of the transcription factor delta-lactoferin is involved in the control of its transcriptional activity and stability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
delta-lactoferring is a SUMO substrate.
SUMOylation plays a key role in the posttranslational regulation of delta-lactoferin activity and stability, thus contributing to the control of delta-Lactoferrins antitumoral functions.
delta-lactoferring is a posttranslationaly modified protein, the SUMOylation of which is a novel mechanism that controls its stability and transcription activity.
